campaign_note: DLL side-loading flaw abused by ClickFix operators (Romulus platform) who bundle a legitimate signed Siemens Software Center binary with a malicious DLL; Siemens says its own systems and update channels were not compromised, and no victim counts have been published.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Siemens blog post warning of active exploitation, as reported by Help Net Security

evidence.counts_what: IP addresses running the attacker platform (Romulus ClickFix panel) infrastructure; not victims
evidence.measured_by: researchers cited by Help Net Security (Forescout per other coverage)
evidence.quote: The researchers identified six IP addresses running it.

campaign_note: SIP MESSAGE handling flaw (fixed by default in 1.11.3, 2026-08-28) that the maintainer advisory says has been exploited in the wild; no exposure, compromise or victim figures found.

evidence.counts_what: vendor statement of in-the-wild exploitation; no count
evidence.quote: Exploitation of this path has been observed in the wild.

campaign_note: SAML/MFA bypass affecting SSL VPN only where SAML login is enabled; SonicWall PSIRT cites a single report of potential exploitation and neither SonicWall nor CISA has shared attack details.

first_exploitation_claim.source: SonicWall PSIRT advisory, as reported by BleepingComputer

evidence.counts_what: vendor statement of a report of potential exploitation; no count
evidence.quote: SonicWall PSIRT has investigated a report indicating potential exploitation of this vulnerability.

campaign_note: Upgrade-window race condition fixed in WordPress 7.1.4 (2026-10-28); Wordfence reports blocked attack attempts and CISA confirmed exploitation, but no source reports a confirmed successful compromise or a count of affected sites.

first_exploitation_claim.source: CISA KEV addition, reported by BleepingComputer 2026-11-04 (Wordfence's blocked-attack figure was published the preceding weekend, exact day not stated)

evidence.counts_what: attacks targeting this vulnerability blocked by the Wordfence firewall in a 24-hour period (attempts, not compromises)
evidence.measured_by: Wordfence, quoted by BleepingComputer (Wordfence page returned empty on fetch)
evidence.quote: blocked 13,095 attacks targeting this vulnerability in the past 24 hours
